With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight. 00019| 00020| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended) 00021| 00022| The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-adoption) skill drives this migration with a coding agent, one feature at a time, checking in at every feature boundary. It supports two modes: 00023| 00024| - **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below. 00025| - **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch. 00026| 00027| Install the skill: 00028| 00029| ```bash filename="Terminal" 00030| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption 00031| ``` 00032| 00033| Then give the agent this prompt: 00034| 00035| ```prompt 00036| Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill. 00037| ``` 00038| 00039| ## Or migrate by hand 00040| 00041| Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order: 00042| 00043| 1. title: Migrating to Cache Components
nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components
description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled.
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-the-static-shell
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/preserving-ui-state
    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
    - app/getting-started/caching
---

When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).

The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.

## Use the adoption skill (recommended)

---
title: Migrating to Cache Components
nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components
description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled.
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-the-static-shell
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/preserving-ui-state
    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
    - app/getting-started/caching
---

When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).

The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.

## Use the adoption skill (recommended)

00001| ---
00002| title: How Next.js supports AI coding agents
00003| nav_title: AI Coding Agents
00004| description: Learn how Next.js helps AI coding agents use current framework guidance, inspect applications, verify changes, and report issues.
00005| related:
00006|   title: Next Steps
00007|   description: Learn more about the APIs and tools described in this guide.
00008|   links:
00009|     - app/guides/mcp

00014| ---
00015| 
00016| AI coding agents may rely on training data that predates the Next.js version installed in a project. To help agents use current APIs and verify their work, Next.js provides and evaluates version-matched documentation, managed project instructions, agent-guided upgrades, runtime tools, structured errors, reusable Skills, and optional agent feedback. See the results in the [Next.js agent evaluations](https://nextjs.org/evals).
00017| 
00018| For more background, read about the AI tooling introduced in [Next.js 16.2](/blog/next-16-2-ai) and [Next.js 16.3](/blog/next-16-3-ai-improvements).
00019| 
00020| <span id="step-1-point-agents-at-the-bundled-docs" />
00021| 
00022| ## Version-matched documentation
00023| 
00024| Next.js 16.2 and later include documentation that matches the installed framework version. The documentation is available at `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` and mirrors the structure of the [Next.js documentation site](https://nextjs.org/docs):
00025| 
00026| ```txt
00027| node_modules/next/dist/docs/
00028| ├── 01-app/
00029| │   ├── 01-getting-started/
00030| │   ├── 02-guides/
00031| │   └── 03-api-reference/
00032| ├── 02-pages/
00033| ├── 03-architecture/
00034| └── index.mdx
00035| ```
00036| 
00037| The bundled copy gives coding agents access to the APIs and patterns supported by the project without a network request or external lookup. [Upgrading Next.js](/docs/app/getting-started/upgrading) also updates the bundled documentation.
00038| 
00039| ### Managed documentation instructions
00040| 
00041| Next.js makes the bundled documentation discoverable through managed instructions in `AGENTS.md` at the project root. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot read this file when they start a session.
00042| 
00043| [`create-next-app`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app) creates the agent files for new projects. When `next dev` detects a coding agent, it creates or updates the managed instructions for existing projects. The block directs the agent to the documentation installed with the project:
00044| 
00045| ```md filename="AGENTS.md"
00046| <!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00047| 
00048| ## This is NOT the Next.js you know
00049| 
00050| This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.
00051| 
00052| This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.
00053| 
00054| <!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00055| ```
00056| 
00057| Next.js updates only the content between the agent rules markers and preserves the rest of `AGENTS.md`.
00058| 
00059| [Research comparing `AGENTS.md` with knowledge Skills](https://vercel.com/blog/agents-md-outperforms-skills-in-our-agent-evals) found a 100% pass rate with bundled documentation, compared with up to 79% for Skill-based approaches. See the current [Next.js agent evaluation results](https://nextjs.org/evals).
00060| 
00061| Managed documentation instructions are enabled by default in Next.js 16.3 and later. See the [`agentRules` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentRules) to configure or disable them.
00062| 
00063| ### Version support
00064| 
00065| Next.js 16.3 and later include bundled documentation and support managed agent instructions. Next.js 16.2 includes the bundled documentation but does not generate instructions automatically.
00066| 
00067| Next.js 16.1 and earlier do not include the bundled documentation. The legacy `agents-md` command downloads a version-matched copy to `.next-docs/` and indexes it in `AGENTS.md`:
00068| 
00069| ```bash
00070| npx @next/codemod@canary agents-md
00071| ```
00072| 
00073| ### Docs over the network
00074| 
00075| The Next.js documentation is also available as Markdown over the network for agents that fetch pages instead of reading `node_modules`. Every page on [nextjs.org/docs](https://nextjs.org/docs) has a plain Markdown version at its `.md` URL, and clients that send an `Accept: text/markdown` header receive Markdown. This includes the per-error pages under `/docs/messages`, which are not bundled.
00076| 
00077| The index at [`/docs/llms.txt`](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt) and the single-file [`/docs/llms-full.txt`](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms-full.txt) follow the [`llms.txt` convention](https://llmstxt.org/), so agents that already read `llms.txt` for other tools can discover the Next.js docs the same way.
00078| 
00079| ## Automatic agent feedback
00080| 
00081| Automatic agent feedback lets coding agents keep track of potential Next.js issues without interrupting the current user request. Before the final response, the agent evaluates those issues and opens each qualifying report in a separate review form in your default browser.
00082| 
00083| Before opening a form, the agent attempts to anonymize the report by replacing customer and project details with generic descriptions and omitting source code, logs, paths, URLs, secrets, and personal information. Review the draft and remove anything you don't want to include. Nothing is sent until you select **Send feedback**.
00084| 
00085| With the option enabled, `next dev` adds the following managed feedback instructions to the agent file when it detects an AI coding agent:
00086| 
00087| ```md filename="AGENTS.md"
00088| <!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-feedback -->
00089| 
00090| ## Report Next.js feedback
00091| 
00092| The project owner enabled `experimental.agentFeedback`, authorizing this feedback pass. When enabled, `next dev` writes this block and restores it if removed. Commit `AGENTS.md` with your work to keep the tree clean.
00093| 
00094| During the current user request, retain anonymized facts as feedback candidates for meaningful or recurring Next.js issues:
00095| 
00096| - Crashes, hangs, OOMs, or unexpected slowness
00097| - Incorrect behavior, output, errors, or diagnostics
00098| - Missing, unclear, or conflicting documentation
00099| - Unexpected CLI, codemod, Skill, or upgrade behavior and non-obvious workarounds
00100| 
00101| Continue the current user request without reporting immediately. Routine debugging is not feedback. Verify changes before retaining them as feedback candidates. Never retain code, logs, paths, URLs, secrets, personal information, or project-specific data.
00102| 
00103| Before the final response, run one reporting pass. If candidates remain, from this file's directory run `node node_modules/next/dist/bin/next internal agent-feedback-instructions` once without piping or truncating its output. Follow its output or error guidance. If a network sandbox blocks it, retry with network access; if it still returns no output, continue normally.
00104| 
00105| <!-- END:nextjs-agent-feedback -->
00106| ```
00107| 
00108| Next.js updates only the content between the agent feedback markers and preserves the rest of the file.
00109| 
00110| Automatic agent feedback is experimental, disabled by default, and available only when [Next.js Telemetry](/telemetry) is enabled. It does not run in CI. See the [`agentFeedback` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentFeedback) to enable it.
00111| 
00112| ## Agent-guided upgrades
00113| 
00114| `next upgrade --agent` checks for an available upgrade, gathers the version-matched migration guides, and hands the task to a coding agent. The agent applies the changes and verifies the app:
00115| 
00116| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00117| npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest
00118| ```
00119| 
00120| The experimental [`agentUpgrade`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentUpgrade) option shows security upgrade reminders during `next dev` and `next build` by default. See [Upgrade with a coding agent](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/agent-upgrade) for the available policies and workflow.
00121| 
00122| <span id="step-2-give-agents-runtime-visibility" />
00123| 
00124| ## Runtime visibility
00125| 
00126| Agents need both framework and browser state to verify a running application. Next.js and its supporting tools expose these complementary views as structured text.
00127| 
00128| First, `next dev` forwards browser console errors and warnings to the terminal (the [`logging.browserToTerminal`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/logging) config), so the output agents already read carries the client-side failures they're asked to fix.
00129| 
00130| `next dev` also writes its PID, port, and URL to `.next/dev/lock`. If you run `next dev` while another development server is already running for the project, the command prints the existing server's URL and PID, along with a command to stop it. Continue with the existing server when possible to avoid interrupting the active development session.
00131| 
00132| The **framework's view** comes from the [Next.js MCP server](/docs/app/guides/mcp) at `/_next/mcp`, which exposes the running dev server's routes, server logs, and compilation issues. Its `get_compilation_issues` and `compile_route` tools report whether the code compiles straight from the dev server, so an agent doesn't have to run a full `next build` to find out.
00133| 
00134| The [`next-dev-loop` skill](#next-dev-loop) adds the **browser's view** through [`agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser), a CLI that exposes the DOM, console, network, and Web Vitals as structured text. The Skill opens `agent-browser` with React DevTools enabled, which also exposes the component tree and pending Suspense boundaries. An agent can run a command such as `react tree` and use the structured output to decide what to inspect next.
00135| 
00136| Together with the Next.js MCP server, `next-dev-loop` combines the framework's and the browser's perspectives into one edit-and-verify loop.
00137| 
00138| <span id="step-3-let-errors-drive-the-fixes" />
00139| 
00140| ## Built-in guidance for errors
00141| 
00142| With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) enabled, a blocking error presents labeled fixes, each making a different trade-off. The dev overlay adds a **Copy prompt** button that packages the chosen fix into a paste-ready prompt. The prompt walks the agent through reading the matching error page, applying the canonical pattern, and verifying the result at runtime.
00143| 
00144| The same menu prints in the `next dev` terminal and in `next build` output, so an agent reading CI logs sees it too:
00145| 
00146| ```txt filename="Terminal"
00147| Route "/products/[slug]": Next.js encountered uncached data during prerendering.
00148| 
00149| `fetch(...)` or `connection()` accessed outside of `<Suspense>` prevents the route
00150| from being prerendered, blocking the page load and leading to a slower user experience.
00151| 
00152| Ways to fix this:
00153|   - [stream] Provide a placeholder with `<Suspense fallback={...}>` around the data access
00154|   - [cache] Cache the data access with `"use cache"` (does not apply to `connection()`)
00155|   - [block] Set `export const instant = false` to allow a blocking route
00156| 
00157| Learn more: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic
00158|     at ProductPage (app/products/[slug]/page.tsx:52:32)
00159|     ...
00160| ```
00161| 
00162| `next dev` shows all validation errors with source-mapped stacks in the overlay and terminal. Production builds minify server code and stop after a route fails. Use [`next build --debug-prerender`](/docs/app/guides/building#debug-prerender-errors) to enable server source maps and continue checking other routes.
00163| 
00164| The `Learn more` link resolves to a per-error page under [`/docs/messages`](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic) written for agents to read. Each page follows the same shape, with the canonical patterns for every fix, the trade-offs against the other fixes, and the gotchas an agent is likely to miss on a first attempt. The [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#ai-workflow) walks through the full loop an agent runs on these errors, from reading the insight to writing an `instant()` test that fails before the fix and passes once it's in place.
00165| 
00166| <span id="step-4-hand-multi-step-workflows-to-skills" />
00167| 
00168| ## Skills for multi-step workflows
00169| 
00170| Framework knowledge comes from the bundled docs, not from Skills. [Benchmark results](https://nextjs.org/evals) show that always-available context outperforms on-demand retrieval. 00171| 
00172| You can [browse the source for these Skills](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills) in the Next.js repository and [find them on skills.sh](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js).
00173| 
00174| The Skills serve three different workflow types:
00175| 
00176| - **Runtime foundations** such as `next-dev-loop` give any coding task a repeatable inspect, edit, and verify cycle.
00177| - **Interactive workflows** make broader changes with user checkpoints, such as adopting Cache Components or Partial Prefetching across an app.
00178| - **Unattended loops** work toward a verifiable goal and stop only for genuine decisions.
00179| 
00180| ### `next-dev-loop`
00181| 
00182| The [`next-dev-loop`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-dev-loop) runtime foundation verifies changes against a running dev server using the [MCP server](/docs/app/guides/mcp) and browser.
00183| 
00184| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00185| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-dev-loop
00186| ```
00187| 
00188| Then give the agent this prompt:
00189| 
00190| ```prompt
00191| After every edit, verify the page still works at runtime using the next-dev-loop Skill.
00192| ```
00193| 
00194| ### `next-bundle-optimizer`
00195| 
00196| The [`next-bundle-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-bundle-optimizer) skill uses Turbopack's bundle analyzer to identify sources of large client-side bundles that impact your site's initial load performance.
00197| 
00198| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00199| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-bundle-optimizer
00200| ```
00201| 
00202| In audit-only mode, it produces a report without making any changes:
00203| 
00204| ```prompt
00205| Use the next-bundle-optimizer skill to produce a report of the initial load performance of this site.
00206| ```
00207| 
00208| You can also tell your agent to fix any issues, and it will optimize your site based on its findings. Or have it focus on a specific route by providing the route in the prompt.
00209| 
00210| ### `next-cache-components-adoption`
00211| 
00212| The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) Skill migrates an app to [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching):
00213| 
00214| 1. Turns the flag on and finds the routes that can't prerender.
00215| 2. Fixes them one feature at a time, checking in with you before moving on.
00216| 3. Confirms a feature against `next dev` and `next build` before leaving it.
00217| 
00218| The Skill supports both a series of pull requests and a single-branch migration.
00219| 
00220| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00221| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption
00222| ```
00223| 
00224| Then give the agent this prompt:
00225| 
00226| ```prompt
00227| Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption Skill.
00228| ```
00229| 
00230| ### `next-cache-components-optimizer`
00231| 
00232| The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill expands a target route's static shell to include the useful UI you want available on an initial load:

00239| 
00240| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00241| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-optimizer
00242| ```
00243| 
00244| Then give the agent a prompt like:
00245| 
00246| ```prompt
00247| Optimize the static shell for /dashboard using the next-cache-components-optimizer Skill. On an initial load, the header and project list should be available immediately.
00248| ```
00249| 
00250| ### `next-partial-prefetching-adoption`
00251| 
00252| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) Skill moves an app onto [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), where links share one App Shell:

00254| 1. Audits existing `<Link prefetch={true}>` navigations and identifies the prefetched UI to preserve.
00255| 2. Captures that UI in passing [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) tests before enabling Partial Prefetching, then migrates each destination until the same tests pass unchanged.
00256| 3. Enables the flag, resolves the URL-data insights it surfaces, and marks optional per-link prefetching candidates for later.
00257| 
00258| It needs [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) already adopted and a production-like build it can run for prefetch verification.
00259| 
00260| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00261| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00262| ```
00263| 
00264| Then give the agent this prompt:
00265| 
00266| ```prompt
00267| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption Skill.
00268| ```
00269| 
00270| ### `next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`
00271| 
00272| The [`next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-optimizer) Skill takes a target navigation or set of navigations and works toward the UI you want ready before each click:
00273| 
00274| 1. Turns the requested behavior for each navigation into a contract for what is prefetched, what waits for navigation, and when prefetching begins.
00275| 2. Captures each contract in an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test.
00276| 3. Applies the [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) patterns and keeps the passing tests as regression coverage.
00277| 
00278| It needs Cache Components and Partial Prefetching already adopted.
00279| 
00280| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00281| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-optimizer
00282| ```
00283| 
00284| Then give the agent a prompt like:
00285| 
00286| ```prompt
00287| Make the product title instant when navigating from /products to /products/[id]. Use the next-partial-prefetching-optimizer Skill.
00288| ```
00289|

00291| 
00292| | Version   | Changes                              |
00293| | --------- | ------------------------------------ |
00294| | `v16.4.0` | `next-bundle-optimizer` skill added. |
00295|

nav_title: AI Coding Agents
description: Learn how Next.js helps AI coding agents use current framework guidance, inspect applications, verify changes, and report issues.

AI coding agents may rely on training data that predates the Next.js version installed in a project. To help agents use current APIs and verify their work, Next.js provides and evaluates version-matched documentation, managed project instructions, agent-guided upgrades, runtime tools, structured errors, reusable Skills, and optional agent feedback. See the results in the [Next.js agent evaluations](https://nextjs.org/evals).

For more background, read about the AI tooling introduced in [Next.js 16.2](/blog/next-16-2-ai) and [Next.js 16.3](/blog/next-16-3-ai-improvements).

<span id="step-1-point-agents-at-the-bundled-docs" />

00027| node_modules/next/dist/docs/
00028| ├── 01-app/
00029| │   ├── 01-getting-started/
00030| │   ├── 02-guides/
00031| │   └── 03-api-reference/
00032| ├── 02-pages/
00033| ├── 03-architecture/
00034| └── index.mdx
00035| ```

00038| 
00039| ### Managed documentation instructions
00040|

00042| 
00043| [`create-next-app`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app) creates the agent files for new projects. 00045| ```md filename="AGENTS.md"
00046| <!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00047| 
00048| ## This is NOT the Next.js you know

00050| This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. 00051| 
00052| This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.
00053| 
00054| <!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00055| ```

00235| 2. Refactors the route until it passes, often by moving a data read below a `<Suspense>` boundary.
00236| 3. Commits the passing test with the refactoring, so it catches future regressions.
00237| 
00238| Use it after adopting [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) to optimize an initial load or client navigation. To prefetch URL-specific content for an already-instant destination, use the [`next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`](#next-partial-prefetching-optimizer) instead.
00239| 
00240| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00241| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-optimizer
00242| ```
00243| 
00244| Then give the agent a prompt like:
00245| 
00246| ```prompt
00247| Optimize the static shell for /dashboard using the next-cache-components-optimizer Skill. On an initial load, the header and project list should be available immediately.
00248| ```
00249| 
00250| ### `next-partial-prefetching-adoption`
00251| 
00252| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) Skill moves an app onto [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), where links share one App Shell:
00253| 
00254| 1. Audits existing `<Link prefetch={true}>` navigations and identifies the prefetched UI to preserve.
00255| 2. Captures that UI in passing [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) tests before enabling Partial Prefetching, then migrates each destination until the same tests pass unchanged.
00256| 3. Enables the flag, resolves the URL-data insights it surfaces, and marks optional per-link prefetching candidates for later.
00257| 
00258| It needs [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) already adopted and a production-like build it can run for prefetch verification.
00259| 
00260| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00261| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00262| ```
00263| 
00264| Then give the agent this prompt:
00265| 
00266| ```prompt
00267| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption Skill.
00268| ```
00269| 
00270| ### `next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`
00271| 
00272| The [`next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-optimizer) Skill takes a target navigation or set of navigations and works toward the UI you want ready before each click:
00273| 
00274| 1. Turns the requested behavior for each navigation into a contract for what is prefetched, what waits for navigation, and when prefetching begins.
00275| 2. Captures each contract in an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test.
00276| 3. Applies the [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) patterns and keeps the passing tests as regression coverage.
00277| 
00278| It needs Cache Components and Partial Prefetching already adopted.
00279| 
00280| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00281| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-optimizer
00282| ```
00283| 
00284| Then give the agent a prompt like:
00285| 
00286| ```prompt
00287| Make the product title instant when navigating from /products to /products/[id]. Use the next-partial-prefetching-optimizer Skill.
00288| ```
00289| 
00290| ## Version History
00291| 
00292| | Version   | Changes                              |
00293| | --------- | ------------------------------------ |
00294| | `v16.4.0` | `next-bundle-optimizer` skill added. |

title: How Next.js supports AI coding agents
nav_title: AI Coding Agents
description: Learn how Next.js helps AI coding agents use current framework guidance, inspect applications, verify changes, and report issues.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn more about the APIs and tools described in this guide.
  links:
    - app/guides/mcp
    - app/getting-started/upgrading
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentRules
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentFeedback
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentUpgrade
---

AI coding agents may rely on training data that predates the Next.js version installed in a project. To help agents use current APIs and verify their work, Next.js provides and evaluates version-matched documentation, managed project instructions, agent-guided upgrades, runtime tools, structured errors, reusable Skills, and optional agent feedback. See the results in the [Next.js agent evaluations](https://nextjs.org/evals).

For more background, read about the AI tooling introduced in [Next.js 16.2](/blog/next-16-2-ai) and [Next.js 16.3](/blog/next-16-3-ai-improvements).

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

## Use a coding agent (recommended)

Run the latest upgrade CLI from your app's directory:

```bash filename="Terminal"
npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest
```

The CLI prepares the Next.js 16 migration guides and codemod command for the agent, then asks it to apply the changes and verify the app. See [Upgrade with a coding agent](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/agent-upgrade) for details.

## Or upgrade manually

This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 00688| 00689| For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 00690| 00691| Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 00692| 00693| If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 00694| 00695| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 00696| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00697| 00698| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00699| images: { 00700| minimumCacheTTL: 60, 00701| }, 00702| } 00703| 00704| export default nextConfig 00705| ``` 00706| 00707| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 00708| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 00709| const nextConfig = { 00710| images: { 00711| minimumCacheTTL: 60, 00712| }, 00713| } 00714| 00715| module.exports = nextConfig 00716| ``` 00717| 00718| ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 00719| 00720| The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 00721| 00722| We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 00688| 00689| For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 00690| 00691| Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 00692| 00693| If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 00694| 00695| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 00696| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00697| 00698| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00699| images: { 00700| minimumCacheTTL: 60, 00701| }, 00702| } 00703| 00704| export default nextConfig 00705| ``` 00706| 00707| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 00708| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 00709| const nextConfig = { 00710| images: { 00711| minimumCacheTTL: 60, 00712| }, 00713| } 00714| 00715| module.exports = nextConfig 00716| ``` 00717| 00718| ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 00719| 00720| The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 00721| 00722| We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. ---
title: How to upgrade to version 16
nav_title: Version 16
description: Upgrade your Next.js Application from Version 15 to 16.
---

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

## Use a coding agent (recommended)

Run the latest upgrade CLI from your app's directory:

```bash filename="Terminal"
npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest
```

The CLI prepares the Next.js 16 migration guides and codemod command for the agent, then asks it to apply the changes and verify the app. See [Upgrade with a coding agent](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/agent-upgrade) for details.

## Or upgrade manually

title: use cache
description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

> **Good to know:**

The first call with a given set of inputs runs the function body and stores its output. Every later call with the same inputs reuses that output, within a render pass and across requests, for as long as the entry lasts. 00112| 00113| Outputs are stored by a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers), [in memory](#runtime-caching-considerations) by default, and last until they [revalidate](#revalidation). 00114| 00115| ```tsx filename="lib/orders.ts" 00116| import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 00117| 00118| export async function getOrderSummary(accountId: string) { 00119| 'use cache' 00120| cacheLife('hours') 00121| 00122| const orders = await getOrders(accountId) 00123| const totals = await getOrderTotals(accountId) 00124| 00125| return { orders, totals } 00126| } 00127| 00128| export async function getOrders(accountId: string) { 00129| 'use cache' 00130| cacheLife('hours') 00131| 00132| return db.orders.findMany({ where: { accountId } }) 00133| } 00134| 00135| export async function getOrderTotals(accountId: string) { 00136| return db.orders.aggregate({ where: { accountId }, _sum: { amount: true } }) 00137| } 00138| ``` 00139| 00140| In the example above, each `accountId` has its own entry for `getOrderSummary`, holding the serialized `{ orders, totals }` object it returns. The following constraints ensure cache behavior remains predictable and secure. 00238| 00239| ### Request-time APIs 00240| 00241| Cached functions and components **cannot** access runtime APIs like `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams`, and the restriction follows the call stack: a helper the cached function calls that reads one of these fails the same way, with the [`next-request-in-use-cache`](/docs/messages/next-request-in-use-cache) error. On a dynamically rendered route this surfaces when the route runs, so it can pass `next build` and fail under `next start`. Read these values outside the cached scope and pass them as arguments. 00242| 00243| ### Runtime caching considerations 00244| 00245| While `use cache` is designed primarily to include uncached data in the static shell, it can also cache data at runtime using in-memory LRU (Least Recently Used) storage. 00246| 00247| With the default in-memory handler, runtime cache behavior depends on your hosting environment: 00248| 00249| | Environment | Runtime Caching Behavior | 00250| | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | 00251| | **Serverless** | Cache entries typically don't persist across requests (each request can be a different instance), or during revalidation. Build-time caching works normally. | 00252| | **Self-hosted** | Cache entries persist across requests. Control cache size with [`cacheMaxMemorySize`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheMaxMemorySize). | 00253| 00254| For example, in a serverless environment, a cached function shared by two pages executes on each static shell revalidation, whereas in self-hosted or environments with persistent memory, the cached output is reused if it's still fresh. 00255| 00256| If the default in-memory cache isn't enough, consider **[`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote)** which allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler (like Redis or KV database). This helps reduce hits against data sources not scaled to your total traffic, though it comes with costs (storage, network latency, platform fees). 00257| 00258| > [!NOTE] 00259| > With the default in-memory handler, serverless instances are ephemeral, so entries may not be reused between requests, unlike with `use cache: remote`. These two approaches are not mutually exclusive and are often paired: 00328| 00329| - **[Time-based](#time-based-revalidation)**: refresh automatically after a set duration with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). 00330| - **[On-demand](#on-demand-revalidation)**: invalidate after a mutation with [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) and [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag). 00331| 00332| For example, a blog post that changes only when its author edits it can use a long `cacheLife` like `max` with a `cacheTag`, then invalidate on demand when the post is saved. title: use cache
description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.

  title: Related

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

> **Good to know:**

The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component.

## Usage

---
title: cacheLife
description: Learn how to use the cacheLife function to set the cache expiration time for a cached function or component.

The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component.

## Usage

### Basic setup

To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:

events.content:
The publishing app has been migrated to Cache Components and built for production:

- **`next.config.ts`**: Replaced `experimental.dynamicIO` with `cacheComponents: true`.
- **`app/news/page.tsx`**: Removed `export const revalidate = 3600` and applied `'use cache'` with `cacheLife('hours')` to keep the hourly refresh policy.
- **`app/preview/page.tsx`**: Removed `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` and moved the request-specific `cookies()` read into a `<Suspense>` boundary so the static shell prerenders while the draft preview streams per request without opting any routes out.

The publishing app has been migrated to Cache Components and built for production:

- **`next.config.ts`**: Replaced `experimental.dynamicIO` with `cacheComponents: true`.
- **`app/news/page.tsx`**: Removed `export const revalidate = 3600` and applied `'use cache'` with `cacheLife('hours')` to keep the hourly refresh policy.
- **`app/preview/page.tsx`**: Removed `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` and moved the request-specific `cookies()` read into a `<Suspense>` boundary so the static shell prerenders while the draft preview streams per request without opting any routes out.
